name: introduction
# Introduction


### Course description

- This course focuses on programming and data management, with an emphasis on building skills for economic analysis and data science.
- Students will learn how to access and manipulate tabular, text, and social-network data; develop essential computer literacy and reproducible research workflows; and apply these computing skills to real-world big-data scenarios.
- The course uses R and Python and leverages cloud computing for enhanced data processing.

`r fa('globe')` [Course GitHub](https://github.com/DataManagement-Visualization/Fall2026)

The repository contains the public slides, code, notebooks, and datasets used in class. Deadlines and private course materials remain in Canvas.

# Why this course?

Fill in the gaps left by traditional econometrics and methods classes.

- Practical skills with tools that will benefit your future career.
- Neglected skills like how to actually find datasets in the wild and clean them.

Data science skills are highly valuable in private and public sector!

- Data viz, cleaning and wrangling; programming; cloud computation; relational databases; machine learning; etc.

--

> *"In short, we will cover things that I wish someone had taught me when I was finishing my undergraduate
school."*

name: getting-started
# Topics

- *Part 1*: Command Line and Version Control
  - Set up.
  - Command line and the Terminal.
  - Git and GitHub for version control.
- *Part 2*: Programming Essentials and Best Practices
  - Python basics.
  - Pandas, mathematical operations with NumPy.
  - Getting data from different sources: Web scraping.
  - Data ingestion and transformation with SQL: SQLite.

---
# Topics (cont.)

- *Part 3*: Applied Data Science and Machine Learning
  - Supervised Machine Learning.
  - Experiment tracking and Model Management.
  - Developing ML models for Production environments.
  - ML in Economics: Debiased/Orthogonal Machine Learning (optional).
- *Part 4*: AI, Analytics Engineering and Data Visualization
  - Docker, Images and containers for reproducible research.
  - Using Large Language Models (LLMs) and Agentic AI.
  - Data Visualizations and reporting in Dashboards.

---

# Set up Checklist

- For this course, we are mainly going to use [GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/features/codespaces).
- Before next class, I want you to go over the following checklist:

☑ Create a [GitHub](https://github.com/) account.
  - You will soon receive an invitation to the course organization on GitHub.

☑ Create a [DataCamp](https://app.datacamp.com/) account with your Emory email address.



---
# Set up Checklist (cont.)

☑ Get access to [GitHub Education](https://github.com/education/students) benefits and [Microsoft Azure for Students](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students).

☑ Download [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/)
  - This is the integrated development environment (IDE) that we are going to use in this course.
  - Most of the time, we will use its cloud version through [GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/features/codespaces).
